issues.legal_issue: A non-member’s claim for specific performance against a member, accompanied by an ancillary request that a cooperative society approve the transfer, is not a claim against the society through the member.
material_facts: A cooperative society member agreed to sell office premises to a non-member, subject to the society’s approval.
The society did not approve the transfer and required the premises to be offered first to existing members.
The non-member’s main claim in the cooperative court was for specific performance of the agreement; its request that the society approve the transfer was ancillary to that claim.
The cooperative court dismissed the dispute for want of jurisdiction, but the appellate court and the High Court held that the dispute came within the society-dispute jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The non-member’s main claim was not a claim against the society through the member, and the dispute did not fall within the relevant party category under Section 91(1)(b). The High Court’s judgment was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 91(1) of the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act requires both that the dispute be of a kind described in the section and that the parties belong to one of its specified categories. Under Section 91(1)(b), a non-member’s claim against a society through a member is not established merely by adding an ancillary request for the society’s approval when the main claim for specific performance is against the member. The Court distinguished Deccan Merchants Cooperative Bank Ltd. v. Dalichand Jugraj Jain, M/s Leong v. Smt. Jinabhai G. Gulrajami, and Sanwarmal Kejriwal v. Vishwa Cooperative Housing Society Ltd., and referred to O.N. Bhatnagar v. Smt. Rukibai Narsindas.

rule.if: cooperative_court_dispute and claimant_is_nonmember and contract_is_with_member and transfer_requires_society_approval and specific_performance_is_main_relief and society_approval_request_is_ancillary

predicates.cooperative_court_dispute: A claimant brings a dispute before a court exercising jurisdiction over cooperative-society disputes.
predicates.claimant_is_nonmember: The claimant is not a member of the cooperative society.
predicates.contract_is_with_member: The claimant’s contract is with a person who is a member of the cooperative society.
predicates.transfer_requires_society_approval: The parties made the proposed transfer subject to the cooperative society’s approval.
predicates.specific_performance_is_main_relief: The claimant’s principal requested relief is enforcement of the contract against the member.
predicates.society_approval_request_is_ancillary: The claimant also requests that the society approve the transfer, but that request is ancillary to the principal contractual relief.

issues.definition: When a non-member brings a cooperative-society dispute based on a contract with a member, makes specific performance the principal relief, and seeks society approval only as ancillary relief, the claim is not treated as one against the society through the member.
